clue.text: Hurt beyond limit

parts.note: off can mean away from or past a point, as in off the edge
an end is a boundary or limit

explanation.surface: Someone has been pushed too far and is wounded by it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurt someone's feelings is to upset or affront them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Feverish winter month — get cross

parts.note: Feb is February, a winter month in the north
to rile someone is to get them cross

explanation.surface: February's chill leaves someone hot, ill and irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Febrile means relating to a fever, and figuratively nervously excited.

clue.text: Cut up and left gutted — praise needed

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: to axe something is to cut it

indicators.note: gutted removes the insides, keeping only the first and last letters of left

explanation.surface: After cutting something and leaving it disembowelled, some compliments are due.
explanation.definitionFit: To glorify or extol someone is to praise them highly.

clue.text: Loss of Trident disastrous, this person held

indicators.note: the scrambled letters hold the pronoun inside them
a disastrous outcome leaves the letters of Trident wrecked and reordered

parts.note: this person is the setter, me

explanation.surface: Britain's nuclear deterrent being lost would be a catastrophe for the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signalled by 'disastrous' gives DETRINT, split by 'held'. Trident is the UK's submarine-launched nuclear missile system, so the surface reads as defence news.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm or damage suffered is a loss, as in to the detriment of.

clue.text: Formula for making stew in cowboy territory

parts.note: WILD signals an anagram and WEST is the fodder, so the phrase as wordplay rearranges those letters into a pot of food

explanation.surface: A recipe for a frontier stew eaten out on the range.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer itself reads as an instruction, 'wild' being an anagram signal applied to WEST, which yields STEW.
explanation.definitionFit: The American frontier of the nineteenth century was the land of cattle drives and gunslingers.

clue.text: Cake seminar's finale given by one talking imprecisely

parts.note: a waffle is a batter cake cooked in a grid iron

indicators.note: the finale of seminar's is its last letter

explanation.surface: At the end of a seminar, cake is handed out by a rambling speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rambles vaguely without saying much is in British usage said to waffle.

clue.text: Yobs given hits, having got caught out

indicators.note: out says the abbreviation for caught is removed from the word

parts.note: clouts are heavy blows or hits
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Thugs are dealt blows after being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: Yob is British slang for a rowdy, aggressive youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Boorish, uncouth young men are synonymous with British yobs.

clue.text: See 13
Newspaper selling fewer copies? Dark times from now on

parts.note: the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
circulation down means sales have fallen

explanation.surface: A paper's sales are falling, so the outlook is gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk, when the sun sets, marks the time after which it is dark.

clue.text: Awkwardly feed a stubborn ass?

indicators.note: done awkwardly, the letters of the words that follow are clumsily jumbled

explanation.surface: Trying to give food to an obstinate donkey is a clumsy business.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey is a classic example of an animal used to carry loads, hence the question mark.

clue.text: One caught in wind — a trying experience that's unfair

indicators.note: the numeral one is trapped inside the wind's name

parts.note: the mistral is a cold northerly wind in southern France
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is swept up in a gale and finds the ordeal unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trying' is a pun: a court case that is tried is literally a trying experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial vitiated by an error in procedure is declared invalid, so the court hearing was unjust.

clue.text: Chemical store exploding — hell ultimately

indicators.note: an explosion blows the word store apart, scattering its letters

parts.note: the letters of store as printed

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of hell

explanation.surface: A shop full of chemicals blows up and all hell breaks loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholesterol belongs to this class of steroid alcohols, a family of organic compounds.

clue.text: The French notice someone living in another's property?

parts.note: les is the French plural definite article
to see something is to notice it

explanation.surface: French people spot a squatter or tenant in somebody else's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenant holding a lease occupies a house owned by the landlord.

clue.text: We fed fleshy dandies to be turned into football team

indicators.note: the words are turned over and transformed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Plump dandies were fed up to become a football side.
explanation.definitionFit: Founded in 1867, this English club takes its name from a Yorkshire city and a weekday.

clue.text: Moving back and yielding not for the first time

parts.note: the prefix re means again, so doing a thing not for the first time
ceding territory is yielding it

explanation.surface: Someone retreating and giving way once again.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairline or tide that withdraws is moving backwards, a participle synonym.

clue.text: Maiden on staff in company attached to the German officer

indicators.note: in a down clue, on puts one piece above the next

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
to staff a post is to man it
der is a German masculine definite article

explanation.surface: A young woman in a firm's workforce linked to a German officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A naval rank between lieutenant and captain, and generally anyone in charge of a unit.

clue.text: Article by journalist offered opposition

parts.note: an article can be a thing or item, an object
ED, short for editor, stands for a journalist in crosswords

explanation.surface: A reporter's piece met with resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a newspaper piece, chiming with 'journalist', but here it means an item.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest against something is to raise opposition to it, a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Bread and cheese served outside old church

indicators.note: the cheese is laid around the other letters

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A ploughman's lunch of bread and cheese laid on outside an ancient church.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich, buttery French yeast roll is a kind of sweet bread.

clue.text: Field worker to hesitate — cloud's beginning to come in

indicators.note: the letter comes in, entering the word for hesitating

parts.note: to dither is to hesitate indecisively

indicators.note: beginning points to the opening letter of cloud's

explanation.surface: A farmhand dithers as the first clouds roll in.
explanation.definitionFit: A labourer who digs and maintains drainage trenches beside fields.

clue.text: Urgent message given when many morris men gather

definitions.meaning: the first of May, traditionally celebrated in England with morris dancing, a folk dance by men with bells and sticks

explanation.surface: A distress call goes out as folk dancers assemble.
explanation.definitionFit: The distress signal comes from French m'aidez, and the spring festival is the first day of the fifth month.

clue.text: Names getting muddled with one having a loss of memory

indicators.note: muddled letters of names are mixed into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone forgetful keeps mixing up names.
explanation.definitionFit: The medical term for a partial or total inability to recall the past.

clue.text: French engineer offers fascinating sight reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as it would be heard, not as written

parts.note: an eyeful is a striking or captivating thing to look at

explanation.surface: A French engineer puts on a spectacle worth watching.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustave Eiffel built the famous Paris tower and the frame of the Statue of Liberty.

clue.text: River runs into track in NI town

indicators.note: the river's letter runs into the track, sitting inside it

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or track
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A stream crosses a path in a Northern Irish town.
explanation.definitionFit: A port town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland, with ferries to Scotland.

clue.text: Showering needed maybe after end of that?

definitions.text: Showering needed maybe after end of that?

indicators.note: after places the rain word behind the single letter
end of picks the final letter of the word that

parts.note: showering of the weather means raining

explanation.surface: After a workout you may well need a shower.
explanation.definitionFit: A gym session or exercise practice leaves one sweaty, so a shower follows it.

clue.text: Steals nothing, as you might say

indicators.note: as you might say tells us the word is judged by its spoken form

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: A thief takes nothing, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to nick something is to pinch or steal it.

clue.text: Prepare for action — so that a form of quoits can be played?

definitions.meaning: ships cleared their decks of clutter before battle; now an idiom for getting ready

definitions.text: so that a form of quoits can be played?
definitions.meaning: deck quoits is a ship game of tossing rings, needing an empty deck

explanation.surface: Getting ready for battle, or tidying a ship for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval idiom for removing obstacles before a fight now means getting ready for any task.

clue.text: Boss has very up-to-date collection of top hats etc

parts.note: the head is the person in charge
gear was 1960s slang for great or fashionable

explanation.surface: A boss owns a trendy array of formal hats.
explanation.definitionFit: Hats, caps and helmets are all items worn on the head, collectively the clothing for that part.

clue.text: Repose with each coming in to sit somewhere else

indicators.note: the abbreviation comes in, sitting inside the word for repose

parts.note: repose and rest are synonyms

explanation.surface: Relaxing by moving everyone to new chairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone in a different chair or seat them again is to move their place.
